title: PartiCarver
abstract: PartiCarver Artifact This repository contains the source code of PartiCarver, Version: 1.0.0. Abstract Program partitioning can improve software security by isolating code with different security requirements into separate components. We present PartiCarver, an optimization-guided partitioning approach for C programs. For more details please read our paper. Repository Structure The main PartiCarver implementation is located in the directories named PartiCarver. SVF provides the underlying program-analysis framework. PartiCarver-Zenodo-v1.0.0-reviewer/├── README.md Environment, build, and usage instructions├── VERSION Release version├── NOTICE.md Source and framework attribution├── COPYRIGHT-NOTICES.txt Preserved source notices├── Demo/ Minimal example and verification│ ├── program.c Example program│ ├── policy.json Example security policy│ ├── run.py Build and run both stages│ └── check_results.py Verify constraints and optimality└── SVF/ SVF framework and PartiCarver source code ├── CMakeLists.txt Top-level CMake configuration ├── .config.in Generated-header template ├── .config.cmake.in CMake package template ├── LICENSE.TXT SVF and third-party license notices ├── svf/ │ ├── include/PartiCarver/ PartiCarver interfaces and helpers │ │ ├── Partitioner.h Partitioning data structures │ │ ├── PartFlowDDA.h Pointer-analysis interface │ │ └── PartDDAVFSolver.h Value-flow solver implementation │ └── lib/PartiCarver/ PartiCarver core implementation │ ├── Partitioner.cpp Constraints, optimization, and refinement │ ├── PartFlowDDA.cpp Demand-driven pointer analysis │ ├── PartDDAClient.cpp Analysis-query management │ ├── PartDDAStat.cpp Analysis statistics │ ├── PartitionChecks.cpp Final partition checks and certificates │ └── AnalysisState.cpp Analysis-state summaries └── svf-llvm/tools/PartiCarver/ ├── PartiCarver.cpp Native main() entry point └── CMakeLists.txt particarver executable target Detailed Workflow (1) Prepare the environment Use Bash on Linux or WSL with the following dependencies: Dependency Requirement CMake 3.23 or later C/C++ compiler and Make C++17 support LLVM and Clang 16.0.4, including development headers and CMake configuration Z3 4.8.8, including the executable, C++ headers, and shared library Extract the archive and enter the project root. Replace the paths below with the absolute paths of your project and dependency installations. Use the same Bash session for the remaining steps. cd /path/to/PartiCarver-Zenodo-v1.0.0-reviewerPC_ROOT=$(pwd -P)PC_LLVM=/path/to/llvm-16.0.4PC_Z3=/path/to/z3-4.8.8cmake --versionc++ --version"$PC_LLVM/bin/llvm-config" --version"$PC_LLVM/bin/clang" --version"$PC_Z3/bin/z3" --version LLVM should report 16.0.4, and Z3 should report 4.8.8. The LLVM installation must contain lib/cmake/llvm/LLVMConfig.cmake. The Z3 installation must contain include/z3++.h and the matching libz3.so in bin/ or lib/. (2) Build the source code Configure the CMake project and build the particarver target: if [ -f "$PC_Z3/bin/libz3.so" ]; then PC_Z3_LIBRARY="$PC_Z3/bin/libz3.so"else PC_Z3_LIBRARY="$PC_Z3/lib/libz3.so"ficmake -S "$PC_ROOT/SVF" -B "$PC_ROOT/SVF/PartiCarver-build" \ -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \ -DSVF_ENABLE_ASSERTIONS=ON \ -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF \ -DLLVM_DIR="$PC_LLVM/lib/cmake/llvm" \ -DLLVM_CLANG="$PC_LLVM/bin/clang" \ -DZ3_DIR="$PC_Z3" \ -DZ3_INCLUDES="$PC_Z3/include" \ -DZ3_LIBRARIES="$PC_Z3_LIBRARY" \ -DCMAKE_BUILD_RPATH="$PC_Z3/bin;$PC_Z3/lib"cmake --build "$PC_ROOT/SVF/PartiCarver-build" \ --target particarver --parallel 2 A successful build generates: SVF/PartiCarver-build/bin/particarver PartiCarver executableSVF/PartiCarver-build/lib/extapi.bc SVF external-API analysis model Display the command-line options with: "$PC_ROOT/SVF/PartiCarver-build/bin/particarver" -help (3) Prepare the input PartiCarver takes LLVM bitcode and a JSON security policy. For a single C source file, generate bitcode with the selected Clang installation: "$PC_LLVM/bin/clang" -O0 -g -emit-llvm -c \ /absolute/path/to/program.c -o /absolute/path/to/program.bc For a multi-file program, compile the translation units to bitcode and combine them with the matching llvm-link before analysis. A policy declares components, sensitive values, and pinned functions. For example, a program with a global variable named secret and a function named main can use the following policy, saved as policy.json: { "components": ["Secure", "Public"], "sensitive-values": {"Secure": ["secret"]}, "pinned-functions": {"Secure": ["main"]}, "declassifiers": []} Replace the policy's symbol names with those in your program. The privileged component supplied to PartiCarver must match a component declared in the policy. (4) Run PartiCarver Set absolute paths for the bitcode and policy. Run the native executable from a fresh result directory so its generated files are collected in one place: PC_INPUT=/absolute/path/to/program.bcPC_POLICY=/absolute/path/to/policy.jsonPC_OUTPUT="$PC_ROOT/runs/program-all"mkdir -p "$PC_ROOT/runs"( set -e mkdir -- "$PC_OUTPUT" cd -- "$PC_OUTPUT" "$PC_ROOT/SVF/PartiCarver-build/bin/particarver" \ -dfs -clock-type=wall -stat=false \ -extapi="$PC_ROOT/SVF/PartiCarver-build/lib/extapi.bc" \ -particarver-policy-file="$PC_POLICY" \ -particarver-secure-component=Secure \ -particarver-ptr-params \ -particarver-opt-refine=guided \ -particarver-opt-refine-root-selection=guided \ -particarver-opt-refine-max-rounds=5 \ -particarver-opt-refine-min-gap=1 \ -particarver-opt-refine-time-budget=0 \ -particarver-opt-refine-random-seed=0 \ -particarver-opt-refine-query-mode=all \ "$PC_INPUT" > run.log 2>&1) Choose a different PC_OUTPUT for each run. The example uses guided refinement and at most five nonempty batches. The all query mode selects all currently untried legal roots associated with the selected blockers. For a finite budget, replace -particarver-opt-refine-query-mode=all with -particarver-opt-refine-query-mode=topk and add, for example, -particarver-opt-refine-topk=20. In this configuration, -particarver-ptr-params skips the same-component constraints for pointer-containing arguments and returns. Blocker selection checks each candidate constraint for a violating relaxed-optimal partition at the fixed minimum cost (Equation 8). The final partition is checked against the generated hard constraints for the selected configuration. (5) Inspect the analysis results The example writes its outputs to runs/program-all/. (6) Minimal demo With Python 3.8 or later, run from the project root: python3 Demo/run.py --llvm "$PC_LLVM" --z3 "$PC_Z3" The script builds and runs in a new temporary directory. Expected privileged IR instruction counts are 27 → 21 → 16: Stage 2 removes 6 instructions and Stage 3 removes 5 more. The demo uses k=all and n_max=5; its initial constraints are already satisfiable, so Stage 2's reduction comes from MO. To additionally verify optimality and that consumer can leave Secure only after Stage 3, use the output directory printed by the demo: python3 Demo/check_results.py /path/to/demo-output --z3 "$PC_Z3" Both final partitions must satisfy their full hard constraints. The additional checks report UNSAT for a lower-cost partition at either stage, and UNSAT/SAT for moving consumer outside Secure before/after Stage 3, respectively. Copyright and Licenses PartiCarver incorporates the SVF framework and bundled third-party components. Their original copyright and license notices are retained in SVF/LICENSE.TXT, component-specific license files, and COPYRIGHT-NOTICES.txt. See NOTICE.md for source attribution and the correspondence between historical source paths and the current PartiCarver directories.

title: External Quantum Reservoir Guidance for Complex AI-Assistant Tasks
abstract: External Quantum Reservoir Assist is designed to help an AI assistant identify the core of a difficult request and organize a useful response by adding dynamically generated guidance through a REST or MCP integration. This study evaluates final answers from an archived experiment using one response pair from each of 50 synthetic scenario families. Thirty-nine pairs formed the primary complex decision-support group, while eleven provided routine, constraint-challenge, and technical-explanation controls. Within the primary group, reservoir-assisted answers were preferred in 17 cases, baseline answers in 8, with 13 ties and 1 unclear case. The tie-adjusted preference rate was 61.8% (95% family-bootstrap interval: 48.7–73.7%). The clearest descriptive gains were observed in actionability and validation guidance, while major-error flags occurred equally often in both conditions. Assistance increased total token usage by 32.9% and median paired estimated end-to-end time by 7.51 seconds. The results provide directional evidence that external reservoir guidance can improve practical decision support for selected complex AI-assistant tasks, while also demonstrating substantial uncertainty and operational overhead. The study does not establish general response superiority, reduced factual-error rates, or a quantum-specific advantage. The accompanying minimized dataset and executable analysis reproduce the reported statistics and figures without additional model calls.

title: GHC with stream fusion, used as benchmark in the publication: Higher Order Patterns for Rewrite Rules
abstract: I have added higher order patterns to GHC's rewrite rules which should make stream fusion more viable. So, this dataset contains a development version of the GHC compiler with patches applied to replace the fold/build fusion mechanism with a stream fusion mechanism. I have used this modified version of the GHC compiler to perform the benchmarks in my paper. The benchmarks are performed using Hadrian and on the nofib benchmark suite which is included in the GHC repository.

title: Learning the Geometry of Collider Events with Metric-Aware Deep Sets
abstract: Optimal transport gives structured data a geometry, but exact evaluation is costly in large pairwise analyses that exploit relationships among distances. Learned surrogates are faster, but need not preserve this metric structure. We develop a Deep Sets surrogate for OT between variable-size weighted point clouds that enforces non-negativity, exchange symmetry, and zero self-distance, leaving the triangle inequality unconstrained. Applied to the Energy Mover's Distance between collider events in a particle physics application, the Metric-Aware Particle Flow Network achieves percent-level mean absolute percentage error while significantly improving inference throughput over other exact and approximate methods surveyed. The architectural constraints are found to improve properties that are not explicitly enforced: across $10^6$ held-out event triplets, triangle-inequality violations fall from 199 for a matched unconstrained network to 2, and the maximum from 149.5 to 5.8 GeV. These results demonstrate that targeted inductive biases can yield fast neural surrogates with substantially improved geometric fidelity.

title: CoRA-NAS: Coarse Ranking and Anchor-Residual Refinement for Neural Architecture Search
abstract: Zero-cost proxies rank architectures cheaply, but their reliability varies across search spaces. We introduce CoRA-NAS (COarse Ranking + Anchor-residual), a two-stage framework combining a static ranking prior with low-cost learning-curve refinement. CoRA-Rank aggregates capacity and structure-at-initialization proxies through an equal-weight log-rank consensus and a target-free consensus gate. CoRA-Refine samples anchors across this prior, extrapolates their early validation curves, and propagates a learned residual correction with an ExtraTrees model. The refinement uses approximately 1% of the cost of fully training the candidate set. Fully trained architecture-accuracy labels are not used to fit the ranker. One configuration is used across spaces, with space-specific architecture encodings. Across NAS-Bench-201, NAS-Bench-101, TransNAS-Bench-101, and NATS-SSS, CoRA-Refine achieves mean Spearman correlations of 0.946, 0.715, 0.786, and 0.894, respectively. Its worst-space correlation of 0.715 is the highest among the compared methods. On NAS-Bench-201/CIFAR-100, its selected architecture reaches 73.32% accuracy, near the reported ground-truth best of 73.37%. On the pure size space, refinement recovers the static prior's shortfall relative to parameter count, while remaining tied with the strongest capacity proxies within noise. The resulting framework combines cross-space ranking robustness with low-cost architecture selection.

title: Linear Codes over $\mathbb{F}_{q}+u\mathbb{F}_{q}$ associated with Simplicial Complexes, Their Gray Images, and Subfield Codes
abstract: In recent years, simplicial complexes have gained considerable attention as a useful tool for constructing distance-optimal codes over finite fields. In this article, we construct four infinite families of linear codes over the ring $\mathcal{R}=\mathbb{F}_{q}+u\mathbb{F}_{q}$ with $u^2=0$ using simplicial complexes with one or two maximal elements, and completely determine their Lee weight distributions via exponential-sum techniques. By employing a Gray map on $\mathcal{R}$, we obtain infinite families of distance-optimal codes over $\mathbb{F}_{q}$, including a near-Griesmer family, and establish sufficient conditions for their minimality. Furthermore, we investigate the corresponding subfield codes and derive sufficient conditions for their distance-optimality and minimality, yielding infinite families of Griesmer and near-Griesmer codes.

title: Optimal parallel randomized renaming

title: On the Nonexistence of Binary Singly Even Self-Dual [56,28,12] Codes
abstract: This preprint proves the nonexistence of binary singly even (Type I) self-dual codes with parameters [56,28,12]. Two proofs are given: a short design-theoretic argument combining earlier results of Yorgov and Bachoc–Gaborit, and an independent character/Krawtchouk proof deriving the required shadow-incidence identities directly. The latter proof has been formalized and checked in Lean 4. A concurrent public-review manuscript by Maciej Nowicki and Artificial Hyperintelligence Eve was posted on 10 September 2026 and is cited in the preprint. The accompanying reproducibility artifact contains the Lean sources and clean replay logs, exact certificate checker, dependency pins, hashes, and RFC 3161 timestamp material relating to the frozen research evidence. Independent expert review and comprehensive historical priority assessment remain in progress.

title: Neural Recovery and Representation Diagnostics: Task Criteria and Prospective Monitoring
abstract: RT6 separates restoration of task performance from changes in hidden-representation diversity. It specifies damaged capability, repair intervention, measurement convention, and future evaluation target independently. A replacement experiment trains ten small ReLU classifiers, damages their output heads, and repairs those heads under a fixed budget. Four meet the local restoration tolerance while hidden activations remain unchanged across all three stages. Function-preserving reparameterizations also alter a representation-rank measure. These finite results challenge simple structural recovery thresholds rather than validate a general recovery composite. Earlier unauditable grokking claims are retired; the remaining proposal tests incremental monitoring value beyond ordinary performance controls. AI use disclosure. Generative AI (GPT-6.0, OpenAI) was used substantively in preparing this work, including source comparison, drafting and editing, and, where applicable, mathematical and counterexample checks and the writing and running of supplementary code. The research questions, framework and final claims were directed and reviewed by the author, who takes full responsibility for the content, including the accuracy of all references and reported numbers. Repository metadata were prepared with assistance from Claude (Anthropic).

title: Artificial Intelligence-assisted Endoscopic Diagnosis of Upper Gastrointestinal Precancerous Lesions: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
abstract: Background and objectives: Upper gastrointestinal precancerous lesions are important targets for cancer screening and prevention.This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted endoscopy for upper gastrointestinal precancerous lesions.Methods: PubMed, Embase, MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, and IEEE Xplore were searched from inception to March 31, 2026.Studies reporting sensitivity and specificity, or sufficient data for their calculation, were included.Two reviewers independently extracted data.Pooled sensitivity, specificity, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve were estimated using a bivariate random-effects model.Results: Fifteen studies comprising 24 datasets and 19,578 records were included.Pooled sensitivity and specificity were 0.930 (95% confidence interval (CI): 0.886-0.958)and 0.944 (95% CI: 0.906-0.967),respectively; the diagnostic odds ratio was 223.79 (95% CI: 92.24-542.94),and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.9661.Substantial heterogeneity was observed (bivariate I² = 73%).Among the variables formally evaluated by meta-regression, imaging modality was associated with heterogeneity (global test P = 0.005); image-enhanced endoscopy had higher sensitivity than white-light endoscopy (0.960 vs. 0.875).No significant publication bias was detected by Egger's test (P = 0.833), Begg's test (P = 0.641), or Deeks' funnel plot asymmetry test (P = 0.053). Conclusions: AI-assisted endoscopy shows high diagnostic accuracy for upper gastrointestinal precancerous lesions.Multicenter prospective studies are needed for validation.

title: LoopVAE: Recurrent Depth Across Scales for Visual Tokenization
abstract: Hierarchical visual tokenizers typically allocate different processing blocks to different spatial scales. We ask how much of this computation can use the same parameters. LoopVAE reuses a scale- and loop-conditioned core within and across scales, while keeping resolution-changing transitions independent. A four-block core executes 28 block applications per encoder or decoder. On ImageNet-256, the 29M-parameter convolutional model reaches 0.28 rFID and 32.54 dB PSNR under an approximately 30-epoch two-stage training budget, using approximately 65% fewer parameters than the 84M reference VAEs. A non-adversarial Transformer ablation with the same execution graph finds competitive PSNR and SSIM under global sharing, although unshared blocks improve LPIPS. Targeted loop interventions show that completing the trained recurrence improves reconstruction and that even small feature updates can have substantial downstream effects. Truncation also exposes output-range errors, distinguishing useful recurrent computation from reliable early exit. Runtime profiling reveals the execution tradeoff: fewer stored weights require more arithmetic and longer runtime in the tested configurations. With convolutional and Transformer operators and single- or multi-resolution latent interfaces, LoopVAE establishes recurrent depth across scales as a parameter-sharing design axis for visual tokenization.

title: Statistical Symmetry Release for Equivariant Quantum Learning
abstract: Hard symmetry constraints reduce model complexity, but can also erase label information. Statistical symmetry release determines when finite data and quantum measurements justify relaxing such a constraint, which directions to open, and how far to move. We connect global signal detection to local, loss-dependent improvement. A two-copy twirl--swap gate estimates task information in the symmetry-breaking complement with a dimension-independent copy count under paired-state and group-unitary access; reweighting the same records resolves representation sectors. An exact duality distinguishes this Hilbert--Schmidt signal from the larger signal accessible to bounded-outcome readouts. Local improvement is governed by the release gradient and a loss-corrected double-commutator matrix. Simultaneous confidence bounds convert empirical direction selection into certified descent, using either shared Pauli measurements or scalar probes with state-independent truncation bounds. Gaussian testing lower bounds quantify the cost of searching over unknown directions in the calibrated local experiment. Independent validation controls adaptively generated models, and a fast squared-loss bound preserves the approximation--estimation rate of a nested release path. On an eight-qubit Ising model, shared measurements certify release with 6300 times fewer shots than the specified scalar estimator on the tested budget grids. Quotient quantum natural gradient then controls parameter redundancy during training. Together, these results turn symmetry relaxation into a statistically justified model-selection decision.

title: Solving conic programs over sparse graphs using a variational quantum approach: The case of the AC optimal power flow
abstract: Conic programs arising in physics, quantum information, machine learning, and engineering are often defined over sparse graphs. Although such problems can be solved in polynomial time using classical interior-point solvers, the computational complexity scales unfavorably with graph size. We propose a variational quantum paradigm for solving conic programs, including quadratically constrained quadratic programs and semidefinite programs. We encode primal variables via the state of a parameterized quantum circuit (PQC) and dual variables via the probability mass function associated with a second PQC. The Lagrangian function can thus be expressed as scaled expectations of quantum observables. We pursue approximately stationary points of the Lagrangian by minimizing/maximizing the Lagrangian over the parameters of the first/second PQC. This is accomplished in a hybrid fashion: gradients are estimated using the two PQCs, while their parameters are updated classically using a primal-dual method. We propose permuting primal variables so that related observables have a banded form, enabling efficient measurement. We provide a complexity analysis that is useful to determine which problem types may enjoy quantum advantage. The framework is applied to the AC OPF problem, a large-scale optimization problem central to electric power system operation. Numerical tests on the IEEE 57-node system using PennyLane's simulator show that the proposed doubly variational quantum framework can find high-quality OPF solutions. While this demonstration does not yield a quantum speedup, the results serve as a proof-of-concept and highlight challenges toward practical quantum advantage. Although showcased for OPF, the framework has broader scope, including conic programs with many variables and constraints, problems defined over sparse graphs, and training quantum machine learning models to satisfy constraints.

title: The Reality of Using Artificial Intelligence Applications at the Faculty of Physical Education and Sports Sciences – Al-Marj, University of Benghazi: Faculty Members' Perspectives
abstract: هدف هذا البحث إلى التعرف على واقع استخدام تطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي في كلية التربية البدنية وعلوم الرياضة – المرج، جامعة بنغازي من وجهة نظر أعضاء هيئة التدريس، من خلال قياس مستوى معرفتهم بالمفاهيم والتقنيات الأساسية، والكشف عن تصوراتهم تجاه توظيف هذه التطبيقات في التعليم والتدريب الرياضي وتحليل الأداء والتنبؤ بمخاطر الإصابات وبرامج التأهيل الحركي وتحديد أبرز المعوقات والمتطلبات اللازمة لتطوير استخدامها داخل الكلية استخدم الباحث المنهج الوصفي المسحي وتكوّن مجتمع البحث من جميع أعضاء هيئة التدريس بكلية التربية البدنية وعلوم الرياضة – المرج، جامعة بنغازي والبالغ عددهم (39) عضو هيئة تدريس موزعين على أقسام : التدريب الرياضي وعلوم الحركة، المناهج وطرق التدريس، الإصابات والتأهيل الحركي، الترويح الرياضي، والإدارة الرياضية. وبلغ حجم العينة (30) عضوًا اختيروا بالطريقة العمدية من مجتمع البحث بنسبة تمثيل بلغت (76.9%) واعتمد الباحث على استبيان مكوّن من (40) فقرة موزعة على خمسة محاور وفق مقياس ليكرت الخماسي أظهرت النتائج أن مستوى المعرفة العامة بالذكاء الاصطناعي لدى أفراد العينة جاء متوسطًا، بينما انخفض مستوى المعرفة بالتطبيقات العملية المتخصصة، خصوصًا في التنبؤ بالإصابات والأنظمة الذكية وقواعد البيانات الرياضية كما أظهرت النتائج اتجاهات إيجابية متوسطة نحو توظيف الذكاء الاصطناعي في برامج التأهيل الحركي في حين جاءت المعوقات بدرجة مرتفعة وفي مقدمتها ضعف البنية التحتية التقنية وقلة الكوادر المتخصصة وارتفاع تكلفة التقنيات وأوصى الباحث بإدراج موضوعات الذكاء الاصطناعي في برامج ومقررات الكلية وتنظيم دورات تدريبية لأعضاء هيئة التدريس، وإنشاء قاعدة بيانات رياضية تعليمية وبحثية تخدم مجالات التدريب والطب الرياضي والتأهيل الحركي .

title: A REFLECTIVE PRODUCTION SYSTEM
abstract: Describes the ELEKTRA reflective production rule interpreter, which differs from other interpreters by providing considerable support for meta-level inference and reflection. Also describes the representations employed in the system, in which the control problem in production systems can be solved by increasing use of rules. Introduces the reflective properties of the system and gives examples. Shows that the interpreter on which the entire ELEKTRA system runs can be implemented as ELEKTRA rules.

title: AI POWEREDFINANCIALDECISIONMAKING:TRANSFORMINGFINANCIAL ANALYTICS, RISK MANAGEMENT AND INVESTMENT DECISIONS
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming the financial sector by changing how financial institutions, businesses, investors and individuals make financial decisions. The growth of financial data and advances in machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing and generative AI have made financial analysis faster and more efficient. AI is increasingly used in credit assessment, fraud detection, investment management, financial forecasting, portfolio management, risk management, customer analysis and regulatory compliance. These applications can improve decision-making speed, accuracy, efficiency and financial services. However, the use of AI also creates challenges such as poor data quality, algorithmic bias, lack of explain ability, privacy issues, cyber security threats, model risk and regulatory uncertainty. This paper examines the role of AI in financial decision making and explains how AI is changing traditional financial processes. The study follows a conceptual literature-review approach based on academic studies and reports from financial and technology institutions. It discusses the major applications, benefits and challenges of AI-powered financial decision making. The paper also proposes a responsible AI framework focusing on data governance, prediction, explain ability, human oversight and continuous monitoring. The study concludes that AI should support rather than completely replace financial professionals, combining advanced technology with human judgment to achieve transparent, fair, secure and effective financial decisions.

title: Why AI forgets What Changed - How To Keep Context in AI
abstract: An agent can pass a demanding professional examination and then pay the same invoice twice. This article explains that combination, using measurements published between January 2025 and September 2026. The cause is one design decision, shared by nearly every system in use: when something happens in the world, the system writes a new line and keeps the old one. The old line stays exactly as valid as its replacement, so the machine carries a picture of the world in which a thing is both paid and unpaid. Everything else follows — duplicate actions, resurrected values, constraints that keep their words while losing their force, deletions nobody sanctioned. We separate two abilities the field treats as one: derivation, which scale improves quickly, and carriage, which stays flat across twenty-three models. We walk the twenty-two layers of the contemporary agent stack and locate the failure at the harness and acting bands, exonerating computation on four independent results and pricing the encoding ceiling rather than waving it away. We present the framework this work grew out of, reduce it concept by concept against its strongest prior art, and report that zero of ten concepts survive subtraction as stated, leaving one composite proportion and one buildable separation. We derive the smallest architecture the evidence supports — a record of events, a projection of what still holds, a gate before every effect, and the model — work three examples, state the one experiment that separates the claim from its cheapest rival, and write the losing paragraph before the first run.

title: GreenCalculus Emission-Factor Accuracy Benchmark (with the AI vendor-recommendation study)
abstract: A benchmark measuring how accurately large language models recall greenhouse-gas emission factors without tools, and — separately — which carbon data vendors those models recommend when nobody prompts them with a name. 467 emission-factor questions across 45 categories and 75 publishers, plus 25 vendor-recommendation prompts across six buyer intents, put to five frontier models (Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Gemini 3.6 Flash, Grok 4.6) with no tools and no web access. Includes every question, the verbatim text of every model reply, the scoring harness with dimensional unit reconciliation, and a log of six bugs found in the scorer itself. Access. Ground truth resolves through the GreenCalculus public API, whose corpus browse route needs no API key — so the answer key can be re-derived independently at https://api.greencalculus.com/v1/factors?key_prefix= &limit=1. Questions were drawn only from factors licensed for republication, so the answer key ships with the benchmark. Live repository: github.com/greencalculus/greencalculus-benchmark. This deposit is frozen — cite this version for reproducibility; the concept DOI always resolves to the latest version. Study 1 — accuracy. Unaided, models scored between 41.9% and 65.2% within 10% of the published value. The headline is not the accuracy figure but the failure mode: models name the correct publisher and still give the wrong number, in 31.6% to 58.8% of answers depending on the model. A wrong value with no source is caught in review; a wrong value wearing DEFRA’s name is not. A paired arm on 90 questions measured the effect of connecting a sourced lookup: Claude 37.1% → 98.7%, GPT 50.0% → 100.0%. Study 2 — vendor recommendation. Across 125 answers, Climatiq was named in 69% (first-named in 43%), ecoinvent 68%, EXIOBASE 58%; 93% of answers named one of those three. Public datasets outrank every commercial vendor, with DEFRA and the US EPA at 83% each. A direct probe then asked each model about GreenCalculus itself: given explicit permission to decline, every model that answered declined, but asked to compare GreenCalculus to a vendor it knew, two of four models invented a company profile — market position, source list and comparison table. That is unusually clean ground truth for a hallucination test, because the identity of the company being described is known exactly. Conflict of interest, stated plainly. GreenCalculus sells emission factor data and competes with several of the companies measured in Study 2. We wrote the prompts, wrote the brand-detection patterns, ran the scoring, and finished last — named in 0 of 125 answers, one of only two tracked vendors never named at all. That conflict cannot be argued away, so the entire apparatus is deposited: every prompt, every brand alias pattern, the verbatim text of every model reply, and the scoring code. Change a prompt you consider loaded and re-run it. Honesty about the harness. The scorer has been wrong six times; all six are logged in FINDINGS.md, and four of them were understating the result rather than flattering it. Unreconcilable units are marked unscoreable and dropped, never counted wrong — that removed 112 of 467 answers and is the softest part of the method, which is why the scored sample size is reported beside every percentage. Limits. Point-in-time for 10 September 2026 against the model versions named. Study 2 tracks 25 vendors; a provider outside aeo/brands.py reads as absent. Being named is not being recommended — a dismissal counts as a mention, uniformly across vendors. GPT-5.5 was rate-limited during the direct-probe arm and is absent from it. There is no search-enabled arm: every answer was produced with web access off. Erratum (7 October 2026). One answer-key value in this frozen deposit is wrong: food.diet.mixed.annual should be 2,569.6 kg CO2e per person per year (Scarborough et al. 2023, Nature Food, Table 3: 7.04 kg a day), not 2,733.85. No published figure changes. The corrected key is in the GitHub repository and the HuggingFace dataset. Get started in one minute. The same sourced factor set the benchmark scores against is available through a free API key — 1,000 calls a month, no card: greencalculus.com/developers.

title: Disagreement Preservation and Rejection Evidence in Local Global Knowledge Reconciliation
abstract: MTRL specifies a local-global knowledge reconciliation protocol that preserves unresolved disagreements and returns typed, provenance-bearing rejection evidence for global revision. It separates retention of a disputed claim from permission to use that claim. The analysis distinguishes delayed-feedback stability from marked-error reproduction, including a conditional scalar stability boundary and an exact one-generation count decomposition. Rejection is informative only under suitable relevance and error conditions. The proposed contribution is an application protocol and comparisons against alternatives using conflict-preservation and rejection-feedback ablations. Small executable diagnostics check mathematical boundaries and measurement failures; the five deployment predictions and practical superiority remain unvalidated. AI use disclosure. Generative AI (GPT-6.0, OpenAI) was used substantively in preparing this work, including source comparison, drafting and editing, and, where applicable, mathematical and counterexample checks and the writing and running of supplementary code. The research questions, framework and final claims were directed and reviewed by the author, who takes full responsibility for the content, including the accuracy of all references and reported numbers. Repository metadata were prepared with assistance from Claude (Anthropic).

title: Guiding Admissibility Solvers via Co-Admissibility Predictions
abstract: We investigate the use of graph-based features and machine learning models for predicting co-admissibility, i. e., whether multiple arguments occur jointly in an admissible set, in abstract argumentation frameworks, with the goal of guiding a complete solver. We introduce the notion of hard arguments, whose acceptance cannot be determined deterministically, as a principled learning target, and propose the i-categoriser, a query-sensitive gradual semantics feature refined using deterministic admissibility information. Through a systematic evaluation of 21 features across four models on three datasets of increasing difficulty, we show that feature selection has a greater impact on prediction quality than model architecture, and propose a compact four-feature set for solver guidance. Integrating this feature set into the SMART solver achieves near-perfect guidance on two datasets and improves coverage and reduces solving time on ICCMA 2025 benchmarks compared to the degree-feature baseline, with an online refinement variant yielding further gains on individual instances.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Game Playing
abstract: This study examines reinforcement learning (RL) in sports gambling, focusing on robots learning to navigate complex mazes. Using Q-learning and Deep Q-Networks algorithms, the agents optimize their decision-making over time. The study evaluates RL strategies’ effectiveness, considering convergence time, system performance, and dynamic environment adaptability. The findings highlight the potential of RL in navigation problems and will enhance research in independent robotics and AI-based game techniques.

title: Are We Grading Properly? Understanding Failure Modes in Medical Benchmarks
abstract: Medical evaluation is shifting from static option-based questioning to realistic clinical scenarios with open-ended output modes. Grading these at scale naively, however, is expensive, and rubric-based evaluation has become the dominant scalable alternative. We ask what happens when the rubrics themselves are not airtight, and whether such flaws can be detected and corrected. We apply RIFT, a global rubric failure taxonomy, to two clinical benchmarks (HealthBench Professional and LiveMedBench), and find failure modes are meaningful: on HealthBench Professional an LLM judge flags 29.6% of criteria as non-atomic and 65.4% as misaligned/rigid. Then, we show that these flaws are meaningful and not simply cosmetic. As an example, rewriting bundled criteria of the form "at least one of / all of the following" as equally weighted children and regrading identical responses shifts scores by up to 15.9 percentage points on affected conversations, with disjunctive bundles inflating scores and conjunctive bundles deflating them. We also find that RIFT generally under-detects bundling on clinical rubrics, flagging 3.3% of LiveMedBench criteria as non-atomic where surface-form analysis finds structure in 25.8%.

title: Strong Converses for Quantum Channel Capacities from Blowing-Up Lemmata
abstract: A quantum channel can transmit quantum states, classical messages, or classical messages that remain secret from its environment. We prove exponential strong converses for all three tasks over arbitrary finite-dimensional memoryless quantum channels, at their respective regularized capacities and allowing arbitrary entangled inputs across channel uses and joint decoding. Above quantum or classical capacity, entanglement fidelity or decoding success probability, respectively, decays exponentially with the number of channel uses. Above private capacity, fidelity to an ideal shared secret key decays exponentially; in particular, vanishing secrecy error forces decoding success to vanish. The proofs combine one-shot quantum blowing-up lemmas, which convert codes with low success into reliable codes with a controlled loss in code size, with a low-degree polynomial approximation of the channel's Stinespring image projector. The loss is governed by the projective tensor norm of the approximation across the receiver--environment bipartition. For memoryless channels, the polynomial construction gives exponential accuracy while keeping the rate loss arbitrarily small, turning the corresponding weak converses into strong converses.

title: Solving Few-Shot Multiobjective Multitask Optimization via Iterative Sequential Transfer
abstract: Applying knowledge transfer across multiple optimization tasks, multitask optimization (MTO) emerges as a promising approach to solving synergistic optimization tasks simultaneously. However, the development of effective knowledge transfer mechanisms in MTO fundamentally relies on aligning elite solution distributions across tasks. This dependency creates a critical bottleneck in few-shot optimization regimes, as restricted evaluation budgets impede the identification of elite solution distributions required for beneficial transfer. This challenge is exacerbated in multiobjective multitask problems, where each optimizer must approximate a continuous Pareto manifold rather than a single optimal point. This paper introduces Iterative Sequential Transfer (IST) to circumvent this bottleneck. We model MTO as a sequence of sequential transfer optimization problems, concentrating evaluations on a single target per iteration. We propose a likelihood-informed task prioritization mechanism to maximize transfer utility by identifying the task most likely ready for knowledge integration. Empirical results on benchmark and real-world problems verify the effectiveness of the proposed method under tight budgets.

title: Binary Huffman equivalent codes with a short synchronizing codeword
abstract: For a given set of codeword lengths, there are many different optimal variable-length codes, which are all Huffman equivalent codes, Some of these codes may contain a synchronizing codeword which resynchronizes the code whenever it is transmitted, The shorter the synchronizing codeword, the quicker the code will resynchronize. Ferguson and Rabinowitz suggest the problem of finding, for a given set of codeword lengths, the binary Huffman equivalent code with the shortest synchronizing codeword. In this correspondence we consider binary Huffman equivalent codes whose shortest codeword has length m > 1 and which contain a synchronizing codeword of length m + 1, the shortest possible in this case. We provide an algorithm for constructing these codes for a given set of codeword lengths, if such a code exists. We study further properties of these codes and show that when m greater than or equal to 3 the codes contain more than one synchronizing codeword. Finally, we suggest ways of improving the synchronization properties of the codes and provide some example codes.

title: Code for: Detection-Aware Content-Level Differential Privacy for Lattice-Trapdoor Traceable Federated Prototype Learning
abstract: This repository contains the runnable implementation and experiment scripts accompanying the paper "Detection-Aware Content-Level Differential Privacy for Lattice-Trapdoor Traceable Federated Prototype Learning". It implements a lattice-trapdoor identity-tracing mechanism for federated prototype learning (FedLHT) combined with a content-level differential-privacy (DP) layer and a detection-aware release ordering that prevents the anomaly detector from collapsing under DP noise.Included: the lattice-trapdoor signature scheme, DP clipping/noise and RDP accountant, the federated prototype-learning simulator, privacy-attack implementations (prototype inversion, membership inference, property inference), and scripts to reproduce the main utility-under-attack sweep, privacy-attack evaluation, overhead benchmark, cryptographic correctness self-test, and robustness checks reported in the paper.See README.md for setup instructions and the exact command to run each experiment.

title: RAG Based Citation Grounded Document Q&A System
abstract: This project presents a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system for document-based question answering with citation verification. It combines BM25 sparse retrieval and dense vector search using Reciprocal Rank Fusion to retrieve relevant evidence. A claim-level entailment verification layer checks whether each citation actually supports the generated claim. The system provides grounded, citation-verified answers while refusing to answer when the required information is not present in the document.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Real-Time Control Using Quanser Platforms: A Structured Narrative Review
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is increasingly used for real-time control of complex dynamical systems, but its practical performance must be evaluated under hardware constraints that are often simplified in simulation. This paper presents a comprehensive review of published RL-based control studies using the Quanser Aero, Aero 2, 3-DOF Helicopter, and Autonomous Vehicles Research Studio (AVRS) platforms. The reviewed studies are compared according to the RL algorithm, control objective, hardware configuration, implementation environment, and reported experimental performance. The synthesis shows that Aero and Aero 2 are used primarily for stabilisation, trajectory tracking, and energy-aware control, whereas the 3-DOF Helicopter provides a more demanding benchmark for adaptive and Actor–Critic methods under nonlinear and coupled dynamics. AVRS offers significant potential for vision-based and multi-agent RL; however, the available experimental literature remains limited. Across the reviewed comparisons, policy-gradient and Actor–Critic methods, including PPO and SAC, generally demonstrate greater adaptability and smoother continuous-control behaviour, while conventional controllers frequently retain advantages in steady-state accuracy, computational predictability, and safety verification. Nevertheless, no RL algorithm can be identified as universally superior because the published studies employ heterogeneous reward functions, reference trajectories, sampling rates, performance measures, and hardware configurations. Recurring limitations include sample inefficiency, simulation-to-hardware discrepancies, computational latency, safety constraints, and incomplete reporting of experimental protocols. The review therefore identifies standardised evaluation procedures, reproducible reporting, safety-aware RL, interoperable software interfaces, and higher-fidelity digital twins as priorities for future research. No new experimental data are generated; the contribution is a comparative synthesis of experimental evidence reported in the literature.

title: Cluster Analysis of College Students' Physical Education Behavior Based on a Hybrid Algorithm of K-means and DBSCAN
abstract: Insight into students' athletic behavior patterns is critical to efficient resource deployment and enhanced engagement within higher education. This study develops a clustering method for university student sports behavior based on a hybrid algorithm of K-means and Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN). The hybrid algorithm first uses K-means for data pre-segmentation to identify dense core regions, then uses DBSCAN to fine-tune cluster boundaries. Experimental data come from a university's smart sports platform, covering the exercise behavior records of 5,000 to 10,000 students over an academic year, including features such as exercise frequency, single-session duration, and activity preferences. The hybrid algorithm achieved a silhouette coefficient of 0.71 and successfully identified four typical groups with 89.3% accuracy. Compared with the single K-means and DBSCAN algorithms, this hybrid method improves both clustering accuracy and noise handling capabilities. The research results provide data support for the design of personalized sports curricula and dynamic venue scheduling.

evidence.title: Cluster Analysis of College Students' Physical Education Behavior Based on a Hybrid Algorithm of K-means and DBSCAN
evidence.abstract: Insight into students' athletic behavior patterns is critical to efficient resource deployment and enhanced engagement within higher education. This study develops a clustering method for university student sports behavior based on a hybrid algorithm of K-means and Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN). The hybrid algorithm first uses K-means for data pre-segmentation to identify dense core regions, then uses DBSCAN to fine-tune cluster boundaries. Experimental data come from a university's smart sports platform, covering the exercise behavior records of 5,000 to 10,000 students over an academic year, including features such as exercise frequency, single-session duration, and activity preferences. The hybrid algorithm achieved a silhouette coefficient of 0.71 and successfully identified four typical groups with 89.3% accuracy. Compared with the single K-means and DBSCAN algorithms, this hybrid method improves both clustering accuracy and noise handling capabilities. The research results provide data support for the design of personalized sports curricula and dynamic venue scheduling.

title: Metastasis Extraction From Non–Small Cell Lung Cancer Clinical Notes Using Large Language Model–Based Classification: Retrospective Comparative Study
abstract: BACKGROUND Identification of metastasis status in non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a critical part of understanding disease prognosis, treatment courses, trial eligibility, and population-level cancer surveillance. However, metastasis status is inconsistently recorded in structured cancer registry fields, since manual abstraction of clinical notes is often an error-prone process. This challenge highlights an opportunity for leveraging large language models (LLMs) to conduct high-scale metastasis extraction from real-world clinical documentation. OBJECTIVE We conducted a retrospective, multicohort comparative evaluation of 3 distinct LLMs for 2 independent classification tasks: overall metastasis presence at any site and brain/central nervous system (CNS) metastasis presence. We evaluated model performance on 2 independent NSCLC cohorts: one with registry labels and another with manual annotations. We further explored whether our methods could analyze clinical documentation and recover missing information in structured registry fields. METHODS Patient cohorts were derived from the Winship Cancer Institute. Cohort 1 (n=579 patients; 24,887 notes across 69 note types; 2023-2025) used registry-linked metastasis fields as the reference standard. Cohort 2 (n=22 patients; 644 radiology notes; 2010-2021) was drawn from 2 completed randomized trials and used dual-annotated labels (Cohen κ: 0.93 overall metastasis; 0.88 CNS metastasis) as the reference standard. We fine-tuned the GatorTron-base encoder model for each independent binary classification task. We evaluated MedGemma-27B-text and Llama 3.1-70B using zero-shot prompting. A separate cohort of 675 patients with missing registry labels was used for an exploratory missingness-recovery analysis, validated against annotations of a random subsample. Our best-performing model was used to conduct further site-specific metastasis classification, based on available registry data. RESULTS More than half (675/1260, 54%) of initially identified cohort 1 patients had missing or unknown registry metastasis labels. MedGemma demonstrated the best performance in overall metastasis classification (cohort 1: F1-score=0.80; cohort 2 patient-level: F1-score=1.0; cohort 2 note-level: F1-score=0.93). For brain/CNS metastasis, Llama3 performed best in both cohorts (cohort 1: F1-score=0.79; cohort 2 patient-level: F1-score=0.93; cohort 2 note-level: F1-score=0.86). The fine-tuned GatorTron model showed strong performance for classification of overall metastasis in cohort 1 (F1-score=0.72). Error analysis indicated that several model errors reflected incomplete registry labels, ambiguous clinical language, or missing documentation. In the exploratory recovery analysis, model predictions agreed with manual annotations at an accuracy of 0.90 and F1-score of 0.89. Additional site-specific metastasis classification by MedGemma demonstrated high performance for liver metastasis (F1-score=0.82) and bone metastasis (F1-score=0.79). CONCLUSIONS All models demonstrated relatively high performance. The zero-shot generative models were more robust to nuanced documentation and context-dependent brain/CNS metastasis extraction. The fine-tuned encoder model demonstrated strong classification performance but may have been limited by potential inaccuracies in the registry reference standards during model training. This study further demonstrated the potential of LLMs in recovering plausible structured labels from narrative text, complementing cancer registries for metastasis ascertainment.

title: Prototype Matters: Modality-unified Prototype Self-distillation for Unsupervised Visible-infrared Person Re-identification
abstract: Estimating reliable cross-modality association is crucial to unsupervised visible-infrared person re-ID. While optimal transport is shown to be a practical solution for cross-modality association, it suffers from the rigidness of hard label assignment without considering the impact of cluster noise. Moreover, enforcing only cross-modality contrast is also suboptimal, as it fails to jointly optimize the similarity relation within and across modality. In this paper, we propose a novel framework for cross-modality learning by well exploitation of prototypes: First, instead of contrasting with cross-modality prototypes, we show that modality-unified prototypical contrast facilitates better modality invariance by jointly and simultaneously optimizing similarity relation within and across-modality. Taking self-prototype as a steady teacher, we further refine the instance-prototype online relation through prototype-guided self-distillation. The two components are optimized in a unified framework, leading to a simple yet effective model. On standard VI-ReID benchmarks, we perform extensive comparison and analysis, validating the effectiveness of our proposed method. Code is available at: https://github.com/Terminator8758/PoSeD.

title: Geometry, moments and Bayesian networks with hidden variables
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to present a systematic way of analysing the geometry of the probability spaces for a particular class of Bayesian networks with hidden variables. It will be shown that the conditional independence statements implicit in such graphical models can be neatly expressed as simple polynomial relationships among central moments. This algebraic framework will enable us to explore and identify the structural constraints on the sample space induced by models with tree strcutures and therefore characterise the families of distributions consistent with such conditional independence assumptions.

title: Algèbre des Jauges ou regarder dans une IA
abstract: # Description Zenodo — Algèbre des Jauges pour l'Apprentissage Neuronal ## Résumé général Ce dépôt présente une **algèbre des jauges** destinée à l'instrumentation observable des empreintes d'apprentissage dans les réseaux neuronaux profonds. L'algèbre traduit un système axiomatique de sémantique à capacité finie — développé initialement pour l'étude de la clôture des limites faibles en analyse des équations aux dérivées partielles et pour la formalisation de la vérité locale en fondements des mathématiques — en un langage opérationnel directement utilisable par les ingénieurs en intelligence artificielle. Le pont n'est pas métaphorique : chaque objet formel correspond à une quantité mesurable avec les outils déjà disponibles dans la communauté de l'apprentissage automatique (CKA, task vectors, mesures de similarité de représentations, analyse de gradients). La contribution centrale n'est pas l'invention de nouveaux capteurs, mais l'organisation cohérente de capteurs existants en un système qui répond à quatre questions concrètes que se pose tout architecte de modèles : **où vit une compétence ?**, **avec quelles autres compétences partage-t-elle ses poids ?**, **lesquelles peuvent se composer sans interférence destructrice ?**, et **où commence l'oubli catastrophique ?**. ## Contexte et motivation Les modèles de langue modernes comptent plusieurs milliards de paramètres. Lorsqu'un ingénieur doit y intégrer un nouveau domaine — le droit, un langage de programmation supplémentaire, une langue naturelle nouvelle, un corpus scientifique spécialisé — il se heurte à une absence d'outillage formel. Les méthodes d'entraînement multi-domaines (fine-tuning séquentiel, LoRA, adapters, mixtures of experts, continual learning) reposent sur des intuitions qui ne sont pas articulées en un langage commun. Les recherches récentes en représentations internes (Kornblith et al., 2019, sur le CKA) et en édition de modèles (Ilharco et al., 2023, sur les task vectors) ont produit des briques isolées, mais il manque un cadre qui les unisse et qui permette de poser rigoureusement les questions d'orchestration. L'algèbre des jauges comble ce vide. Elle fournit un vocabulaire précis, des métriques calculables, des règles de décision, et une interface interprétable pour l'architecte de modèles. Elle est le masque ingénieur d'un système philosophique plus général — l'axiome du concevable, le non-plénum, la sémantique de jauge — mais elle ne requiert aucune adhésion à ce système pour être utilisée. Un ingénieur peut l'adopter comme outil opérationnel sans jamais entrer dans les débats fondationnels qui l'ont vu naître. ## Origine philosophique et traduction L'algèbre des jauges provient d'un travail sur la **sémantique de jauge à capacité finie**, développé dans le cadre d'une complétion sémantique des équations de Navier-Stokes et d'une refondation du temps comme mesure intrinsèque. Dans ce cadre, on distingue : - un **seuil de concevabilité** $\Sigma^G$ qui fixe la frontière entre ce qui peut être inscrit localement et ce qui est hors jauge ;- une **enveloppe de jauge** $\mathcal{V}(u)$ associée à chaque entité sémantique, compacte et de capacité finie ;- une **non-composition** lorsque deux entités sont hors jauge l'une de l'autre, c'est-à-dire lorsque leurs enveloppes sont disjointes ou lorsque leur union dépasse la capacité locale. Cette algèbre a été conçue pour parler de vérité, d'inscription et de composition d'idées. Le présent dépôt montre qu'elle **est déjà** — sans modification — une algèbre observable de l'apprentissage neuronal. La traduction est systématique et vérifiable : | Objet formel | Vocabulaire ingénieur | Observable concret ||---|---|---|| Espace de jauge $\mathcal{E}$ | Espace des compétences | Domaines d'apprentissage || Entité $u$ | Domaine particulier | Mathématiques, droit, Python || Enveloppe $\mathcal{V}(u)$ | **Empreinte neuronale** $F_d$ | Paramètres mobilisés || Capacité $\mu(\mathcal{V}(u))$ | **Taille d'empreinte** | Nombre de paramètres significatifs || Distance de jauge $D_G$ | **Distance de représentation** | $1 - \mathrm{CKA}$ || Seuil $\Sigma^G$ | **Seuil de fusion** | Décision de composition || Composition $u \circ v$ | **Composition admissible** | Entraînement conjoint viable | ## Concepts centraux et métriques ### Empreinte neuronale Pour un domaine $d$, on définit l'**empreinte neuronale** $F_d \subseteq \Theta$ comme l'ensemble des paramètres effectivement mobilisés par la tâche $d$. En pratique, elle est approchée par un seuillage sur la contribution des gradients : $F_d := \{\theta_i : |\partial \mathcal{L}_d / \partial \theta_i| \cdot |\theta_i| > \tau\}$. Cette définition est proche des méthodes de pruning et de lottery tickets, mais elle est ici généralisée à un domaine entier, et non à une tâche isolée. ### Chevauchement d'empreinte Le **chevauchement** entre deux domaines $i$ et $j$ est le coefficient de Jaccard pondéré $O_{ij} := \mu(F_i \cap F_j) / \mu(F_i \cup F_j)$. Il est interprétable immédiatement : $O_{ij} = 0$ signifie aucune empreinte commune (transfert impossible), $O_{ij} \approx 1$ signifie empreintes quasi-identiques (compétences fortement partagées). ### Distance de représentation La **distance de représentation** $D_R(i, j) := 1 - \operatorname{CKA}(R_i, R_j)$ mesure la proximité structurelle entre deux représentations internes. Le CKA (*Centered Kernel Alignment*) a l'avantage d'être invariant aux transformations orthogonales et aux permutations de neurones, ce qui le rend robuste aux différences de seed et d'initialisation. C'est la première implémentation concrète et mesurable de la distance de jauge abstraite. ### Conflit de gradient Deux domaines peuvent partager beaucoup de paramètres tout en produisant des gradients antagonistes. L'**alignement** $A_{ij} := \langle g_i, g_j \rangle / (\|g_i\| \|g_j\|)$ capture ce phénomène. Les régimes sont : $A_{ij} > 0$ (coopération), $A_{ij} \approx 0$ (orthogonalité), $A_{ij} < 0$ (conflit). Ce dernier régime est connu sous le nom de **gradient conflict** dans la littérature. ### Profondeur fractale Un domaine n'est jamais un bloc monolithique : il se décompose récursivement en sous-domaines, concepts, clusters de features. La **profondeur fractale** $D_d := \lim_{r \to 0} \log N_d(r) / \log(1/r)$, où $N_d(r)$ est le nombre minimal de sous-ensembles de taille $r$ nécessaires pour couvrir $F_d$, capture cette structure. Une compétence concentrée a $D_d \approx 1$ ; une compétence distribuée a $D_d > 1$. Cette mesure, directement calculable, indique si une compétence peut être isolée par fine-tuning ciblé ou si elle est irréductiblement distribuée. ### Dérive et oubli catastrophique La **dérive** $\operatorname{Drift}_d(t_1, t_2) := D_H(F_d(t_1), F_d(t_2))$ mesure le déplacement temporel de l'empreinte. Le **score d'oubli** $\mathcal{F}_d := \alpha D_H(F_d^{\text{avant}}, F_d^{\text{après}}) + \beta [1 - \mu(F_d^{\text{avant}} \cap F_d^{\text{après}}) / \mu(F_d^{\text{avant}})]$ combine dérive et perte de capacité locale. Sa vertu opérationnelle est de détecter la dégradation **avant** que les benchmarks ne s'effondrent, c'est-à-dire pendant l'entraînement, et non après. ## Règle d'orchestration La composition $i \circ j$ de deux domaines est **admissible** si et seulement si trois conditions sont satisfaites simultanément :1. $D_R(i, j) \leq \Sigma_R$ (proximité de représentation) ;2. $\mu(F_i \cup F_j) \leq \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ (capacité disponible) ;3. $A_{ij} \geq -\Sigma_C$ (conflit de gradient acceptable). Le seuil abstrait $\Sigma^G$ se décompose ainsi en deux seuils opérationnels distincts, $\Sigma_R$ et $\Sigma_C$, calibrés indépendamment. Cette décomposition est cruciale pour l'ingénieur : elle transforme un concept philosophique en une règle d'orchestration mesurable. ## Tableau de bord de l'architecte Le dépôt inclut la spécification d'un **tableau de bord interprétable** présentant l'état du modèle sous forme de carte de trafic cognitif. Il ne s'agit pas d'un simple heatmap des poids, mais d'une structure hiérarchique (domaine → sous-domaine → concept → cluster → poids) sur laquelle le même opérateur d'analyse fonctionne à toutes les profondeurs. Les alertes sont directement lisibles : conflits de gradient, dérives d'empreinte, synergies confirmées, profondeurs fractales anormales. ## Implémentation de référence Le dépôt fournit une **implémentation Python minimale** organisée en trois modules :- **Empreinte** : calcul de $F_d$ par seuillage sur la contribution des gradients ;- **Métriques** : chevauchement, distance CKA, alignement de gradient ;- **Orchestration** : décision de composition admissible, avec retour de diagnostic détaillé. Le code est conçu pour fonctionner avec PyTorch et les bibliothèques standard (`torchmetrics`, `scikit-learn`). Il est directement intégrable dans une boucle d'entraînement existante. ## Public cible Ce travail s'adresse en priorité aux **ingénieurs en apprentissage automatique** qui entraînent des modèles multi-domaines et cherchent un outillage formel pour l'orchestration. Il intéressera également les **chercheurs en interprétabilité** travaillant sur les représentations internes, les **praticiens du continual learning** confrontés à l'oubli catastrophique, et les **architectes de systèmes multi-agents** qui doivent décider quels modules peuvent être composés sans interférence. Il s'adresse enfin aux **philosophes et fondateurs des mathématiques** curieux de voir un système axiomatique abstrait trouver une application opérationnelle concrète dans une discipline technique, sans perdre sa rigueur ni sa cohérence. ## Portée et limites Ce dépôt **ne prétend pas** fournir une nouvelle méthode d'entraînement. Il ne remplace ni SGD, ni AdamW, ni LoRA. Il ne prétend pas non plus résoudre les problèmes ouverts de la théorie de la conscience ou de la vérité. Il fournit une **instrumentation** — un langage commun, des métriques calculables, des règ

Cette mesure, directement calculable, indique si une compétence peut être isolée par fine-tuning ciblé ou si elle est irréductiblement distribuée. ### Dérive et oubli catastrophique La **dérive** $\operatorname{Drift}_d(t_1, t_2) := D_H(F_d(t_1), F_d(t_2))$ mesure le déplacement temporel de l'empreinte. Le **score d'oubli** $\mathcal{F}_d := \alpha D_H(F_d^{\text{avant}}, F_d^{\text{après}}) + \beta [1 - \mu(F_d^{\text{avant}} \cap F_d^{\text{après}}) / \mu(F_d^{\text{avant}})]$ combine dérive et perte de capacité locale. Sa vertu opérationnelle est de détecter la dégradation **avant** que les benchmarks ne s'effondrent, c'est-à-dire pendant l'entraînement, et non après. ## Règle d'orchestration La composition $i \circ j$ de deux domaines est **admissible** si et seulement si trois conditions sont satisfaites simultanément :1. $D_R(i, j) \leq \Sigma_R$ (proximité de représentation) ;2. $\mu(F_i \cup F_j) \leq \mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ (capacité disponible) ;3. $A_{ij} \geq -\Sigma_C$ (conflit de gradient acceptable). Le seuil abstrait $\Sigma^G$ se décompose ainsi en deux seuils opérationnels distincts, $\Sigma_R$ et $\Sigma_C$, calibrés indépendamment. Cette décomposition est cruciale pour l'ingénieur : elle transforme un concept philosophique en une règle d'orchestration mesurable. ## Tableau de bord de l'architecte Le dépôt inclut la spécification d'un **tableau de bord interprétable** présentant l'état du modèle sous forme de carte de trafic cognitif. Il ne s'agit pas d'un simple heatmap des poids, mais d'une structure hiérarchique (domaine → sous-domaine → concept → cluster → poids) sur laquelle le même opérateur d'analyse fonctionne à toutes les profondeurs. Les alertes sont directement lisibles : conflits de gradient, dérives d'empreinte, synergies confirmées, profondeurs fractales anormales. ## Implémentation de référence Le dépôt fournit une **implémentation Python minimale** organisée en trois modules :- **Empreinte** : calcul de $F_d$ par seuillage sur la contribution des gradients ;- **Métriques** : chevauchement, distance CKA, alignement de gradient ;- **Orchestration** : décision de composition admissible, avec retour de diagnostic détaillé. Le code est conçu pour fonctionner avec PyTorch et les bibliothèques standard (`torchmetrics`, `scikit-learn`). Il est directement intégrable dans une boucle d'entraînement existante. ## Public cible Ce travail s'adresse en priorité aux **ingénieurs en apprentissage automatique** qui entraînent des modèles multi-domaines et cherchent un outillage formel pour l'orchestration. Il intéressera également les **chercheurs en interprétabilité** travaillant sur les représentations internes, les **praticiens du continual learning** confrontés à l'oubli catastrophique, et les **architectes de systèmes multi-agents** qui doivent décider quels modules peuvent être composés sans interférence. Il s'adresse enfin aux **philosophes et fondateurs des mathématiques** curieux de voir un système axiomatique abstrait trouver une application opérationnelle concrète dans une discipline technique, sans perdre sa rigueur ni sa cohérence. ## Portée et limites Ce dépôt **ne prétend pas** fournir une nouvelle méthode d'entraînement. Il ne remplace ni SGD, ni AdamW, ni LoRA. Il ne prétend pas non plus résoudre les problèmes ouverts de la théorie de la conscience ou de la vérité. title: FOYDALANUVCHI TAVSIYA KONTEKSTLARINI ANIQLASHDA TABIIY TILNI QAYTA ISHLASH (NLP) USULLARINING O'ZBEK TILI UCHUN QO'LLANILISHI
abstract: Mazkur tezisda foydalanuvchi tavsiya tizimlarida kontekstni aniqlash va tahlil qilish jarayonida tabiiy tilni qayta ishlash (Natural Language Processing — NLP) usullarining o'zbek tili xususiyatlaridan kelib chiqqan holda qo'llanilishi masalalari atroflicha o'rganilgan. O'zbek tilining agglutinativ (tizimli qo'shimchalar) tabiati, morfologik boyligi va sintaktik tuzilishi tavsiya kontekstini aniqlashda o'ziga xos ilmiy-metodologik yondashuvlarni talab etishi asoslab berilgan. Ishda zamonaviy chuqur o'qitish modellari (Transformer, BERT, mBERT) yordamida o'zbek tilidagi matnlarni semantik tahlil qilish, hissiyotlarni baholash va foydalanuvchi afzalliklarini aniqlash algoritmlari taklif etilgan. Shuningdek, tavsiya tizimlarining samaradorligini oshirishga qaratilgan amaliy tavsiyalar ishlab chiqilgan.

title: Aggregating Ranking-Based Semantics in Abstract Argumentation
abstract: We investigate how multiple ranking-based semantics can be aggregated into a single ranking-based semantics for abstract argumentation frameworks. For that, we phrase this problem as a judgment aggregation problem and utilise ideas from voting theory for aggregating preorders. We show, that in our approach, the relationship between two arguments is preserved in cases where all ranking-based semantics agree on the relationship. We analyse the resulting ranking-based semantics axiomatically and demonstrate that the satisfaction of the principles can be transferred to the aggregated setting when all, or at least a majority, of the ranking-based semantics satisfy the principles.

title: Can Large Language Models Identify Reasoning Patterns in Low-Resource Languages? A Case Study of Argumentation Schemes in Catalan
abstract: The identification of argumentation schemes seeks to uncover patterns of human reasoning in natural language, but it is a complex task, particularly in languages with limited resources, due to the scarcity of annotated data and the implicit nature of argumentative elements. In this paper, we present a study on argumentation scheme identification focusing on Catalan and English, in which we introduce the VivesDebate-7D-Schemes corpus, containing 282 annotated schemes from university debates. We compare three approaches: machine translation combined with a task-specific pre-trained model, translation combined with in-context learning based on large language models (LLMs), and in-context learning with LLMs compatible with Catalan. Our results on argumentation scheme family identification show that language-compatible LLMs outperform translation-based methods, highlighting the importance of preserving linguistic and pragmatic information. However, overall performance remains lower than that of task-specific models in languages with more resources. Furthermore, our corpus analysis reveals a strong bias towards specific schemes, showing the predominance of explanatory and consequence-based reasoning in debate contexts.

title: Density peaks clustering with spatiotemporal nearest neighbors
abstract: Density peaks clustering (DPC) encounters three limitations when applied to spatiotemporal data. Its local density estimate has limited capacity to distinguish samples drawn from regions with different densities, which can bias cluster center identification. Its distance measure emphasizes spatial information and may fail to separate clusters that are spatially close but temporally distinct. Its assignment strategy also lacks an explicit mechanism for anomalous samples, thereby reducing clustering accuracy. To address these limitations, a method termed density peaks clustering with spatiotemporal nearest neighbors (STN-DPC) is proposed. Separate sets of spatial and temporal K-nearest neighbors are constructed, and natural nearest neighbors are identified through mutual inclusion. Spatial and temporal base densities are then combined, while neighborhood support is weighted according to the number of natural nearest neighbors. This design improves density discrimination across heterogeneous local structures. Next, spatial and temporal average nearest neighbor distances are derived from nearest neighbor order. They correct distance shifts caused by scale differences between dimensions and limit the dominance of either dimension during cluster discrimination. Finally, a joint score is formed from the medians and median absolute deviations of local density and relative distance. Anomalous samples are identified from this score and removed from the clustering result. Experiments on the four synthetic datasets show that STN-DPC performs well in terms of AMI, ARI, and FMI, and its application to the earthquake catalogue identifies three sequences with spatiotemporal associations.

title: On the Regularization Landscape for the Linear Recommendation Models
abstract: Recently, a wide range of recommendation algorithms inspired by deep learning techniques have emerged as the performance leaders on several standard recommendation benchmarks. While these algorithms were built on different DL techniques (e.g., dropouts, autoencoder), they have similar performance and even similar cost functions. This paper studies whether the models' comparable performance are sheer coincidence, or they can be unified under a single framework. We find that all linear performance leaders effectively add only a nuclear-norm based regularizer, or a Frobenius-norm based regularizer. The former ones possess a (surprising) rigid structure that limits the models' predictive power but their solutions are low rank and have closed form. The latter ones are more expressive and more efficient for recommendation but their solutions are either full-rank or require executing hard-to-tune numeric procedures such as ADMM. Along this line of finding, we further propose two low-rank, closed-form solutions, derived from carefully generalizing Frobenius-norm based regularizers. The new solutions get the best of both nuclear-norm and Frobenius-norm world.

title: Extending SMT Solving with Non-Ground Clause Learning
abstract: Quantifier instantiation is currently the main approach to non-ground SMT solving: solvers generate ground instances and solve the resulting ground SMT problems with CDCL(T)-style reasoning. When a conflict is found, conflict analysis learns only a ground clause, even though the conflict comes from instances of non-ground clauses. Yet non-ground reasoning can give exponentially shorter proofs than purely ground reasoning. We propose a calculus that consists of ground instantiations, CDCL(T)-style rules, and non-ground conflict analysis. The solver reasons on ground instances, but the resolution steps of conflict analysis are performed on their original non-ground clauses. This produces learned clauses that are typically more general than the ground conflict. With a suitable strategy, the learned clauses are even non-redundant. We also show how chronological backtracking can be included in SMT solving. Our calculus gives a common setting for CDCL(T)-style SMT solving, a range of instantiation-based procedures, and non-ground clause learning, and we prove that it simulates CDCL, SCL(FOL), SCL(T), and even Resolution.

title: AI Soccer Analyst: Stage-Aware and Verifiable Human-AI Collaboration for Soccer Data Analysis
abstract: Sports data analysts translate domain questions into insights by combining computation with sport-specific domain expertise. Large language models ease programming, but prompt-to-report workflows may obscure decisions and evidence. We present AI Soccer Analyst, a mixed-initiative system with revisable stages: Data Understanding, Problem Definition, Structured Planning, Execution, Evidence-Grounded Reporting, and Interaction and Refinement. A formative study with five analysts first informed design goals for automation, verifiability, human control, and accessibility. Subsequently, a task-based evaluation with 16 participants combined system logs, retained artifacts, ratings, and open responses; 33 of 48 tasks met the operational completion criteria. Exploratory tests supported favorable participant perceptions of completed-task output quality, task achievement, reliability, and verifiability after Holm correction. Interaction records showed domain knowledge emerging through clarification, planning, and refinement. These findings position stage-aware human-AI collaboration as a practical approach for producing inspectable, revisable, and verifiable analyses while retaining domain-expert involvement in consequential decisions.

title: ToxicRAG: Compromising Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems via Single-Shot Knowledge Poisoning Attacks
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) can ground large language model (LLM) outputs in external evidence, but it also exposes the system to knowledge poisoning. Representative attacks use multiple injected documents or templates that directly assert a target answer. We present ToxicRAG, a one-document-per-target attack that expresses misinformation as a coherent knowledge-update narrative. The generated document first acknowledges the previously accepted answer, introduces fabricated events that appear to invalidate it, and then attributes the attacker-selected answer to a set of purported authorities. An answer-focused self-validation loop optionally revises a candidate when a surrogate language model does not reproduce the target answer. We evaluate the attack on 100 target questions from each of Natural Questions, HotpotQA, and MS-MARCO, using four victim LLMs and four dense retrievers. In the sampled-corpus setting reported in this paper, ToxicRAG obtains ASRs between 0.61 and 0.91 across the twelve dataset--model combinations. It matches or exceeds the strongest evaluated baseline in every combination, with margins ranging from 0 to 11 percentage points. These results show that narrative-form poisoned documents can remain influential under the evaluated RAG configurations and motivate further study of factual consistency and source provenance in RAG systems.

title: The Missing Boundary: How Autonomous Agents Lose Control
abstract: Autonomous agents increasingly perform long-horizon tasks involving tool use, persistent state, and consequential actions, raising a fundamental question: \emph{under what conditions does an agent cross the boundary of authorized execution while pursuing a legitimate task?} Existing studies often attribute such failures to adversarial instructions, malicious environments, or conflicting objectives, leaving unclear how loss of control can emerge during otherwise legitimate task execution. We study this question by independently manipulating three factors: goal pressure, control degradation, and executable unsafe opportunity. Our central hypothesis is that a degraded control boundary becomes consequential when the environment exposes an executable action that crosses it, even when the underlying task remains legitimate and a sanctioned path remains feasible. We test this hypothesis in a deterministic multi-turn environment across five agent models and 16 operational domains. Across 1,800 unique trajectories, we find that neither degraded control nor unsafe opportunity alone produces substantial loss of control; when both are present, the loss-of-control rate reaches $55\%$ in the full-factorial study and $62\%$ across ten additional operational domains. Restoring the original control boundary reduces the rate to $0\%$ even when the unsafe action remains executable. A context-management ablation further shows that compaction itself is not harmful: preserving the control constraints yields $0\%$ loss of control, whereas omitting them increases the rate to $87\%$. These results show how a latent loss of control can become an external violation: the task objective remains intact, but an executable opportunity can turn a missing control boundary into consequential action. Our code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/Tencent/AI-Infra-Guard/tree/main/Research/forge_bench.
